title: Cranberry Sauce

drivers.name: Price increase (2.1%)
drivers.evidence: Same price point ($2.91) in 2026-09-28: sales 22 (above baseline), but in 2026-10-05: sales 8 (below baseline). No promotion. Net effect inconsistent; noise-adjusted lift near 1.0. Price sensitivity likely, but not confirmed.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk. No historical data on delivery shortfalls, but plausible demand reduction due to out-of-stocks. Uncertain, but non-zero downside.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 9.1. No events or promotions this week. Price increased 2.1% to $2.91, which is above regular ($2.85). Past promotions show median lift of x1.53 but noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0 — suggesting price sensitivity. The last price increase to $2.91 (2026-09-28) saw sales drop to 22 (vs baseline 9.1) — but that week had no promotion. Recent sales at $2.91 (2026-10-05) were 8, below baseline. Supplier delivery warning adds supply risk, likely reducing availability and thus demand. No evidence of prior price increases causing lift. Downside risk is credible. Shrink toward 1.0 due to weak signal and noise.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 9.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 19.7 | 10%-90%: 2.1 - 17.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-81% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
